text:
anya: Hey — saw a spike in token billing for hosted customers tied to streaming reconnect storms this morning. Looks like clients reconnecting after a heartbeat drop were getting counted twice for quota.

kevin: Can you paste the logs or a sample request/response?

anya: Pasted a sanitized example from our edge logs: 
```
REQUEST: GET /v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-4-mini
Headers: Host: api.redwood.ai\n         Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\n         Accept: text/event-stream
RESPONSE: 200 OK\n<event: data> data: {"delta":"hello"}\n\n# client disconnects (network blip) then reconnects immediately with same bearer token
REQUEST: GET /v1/streams/chat?model=gpt-4-mini (new TCP conn)
Headers: same as above
RESPONSE: 200 OK\n<event: data> data: {"delta":" world"}
```

anya: Telemetry shows both sessions got charged for tokens generated (server-side counting per connection + finalization). No idempotency header was present because SSE clients rarely send one.

maria: Ugh. So two problems: (1) our quota accounting ties to connection lifetime rather than a request-level id, (2) console / billing UI shows a user-facing spike without traceability to reconnect events.

sam: Do we have any existing connection dedupe header? We added `X-Request-Id` for REST but SSE replays/reconnects rarely surface it. Could we encourage clients to send a `X-Stream-Conn-Id` or similar?

kevin: Server-side approaches: dedupe by `X-Request-Id` if provided, OR track last-ack sequence per user-token and mark resumed streams as continuation (dedupe accounting). That requires the client to include a resume token or sequence.

anya: Some clients won't change. We should implement defensive server-side heuristics: if a new SSE connection for same bearer appears within 2s of a previous one and no finalization event was emitted, treat as a reconnect and attempt to merge accounting until we see duplicate tokens. But we need to be careful not to undercount genuine parallel streams.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/service-edge-v3 -> prod at 2026-07-22T10:30Z (changes from kevin).

kevin: Plan proposal:
- Short term (hotfix): detect short-window same-token reconnects and mark them as potential resume; don't finalize billing until 5s of idle after last event OR explicit stream-end. Add a `reconnect_penalty` telemetry flag when we applied the heuristic.
- Mid term: add use-case for `X-Stream-Conn-Id` and `X-Stream-Seq` in SDKs and document in API. Update console to show reconnection-penalty metrics per customer.
- Long term: server-side resumable stream protocol with explicit resume tokens and server-provided offsets.

maria: For the console part I can add a small dashboard card: "Reconnect penalty" (gauge + heatmap) and tie to alerts when > 2% of token usage is flagged. I need the metric name and tags.

kevin: Metric we will emit: `streaming.reconnect_penalty.count` with tags `customer_id`, `region`, `heuristic=short_window|explicit_resume`. Also `streaming.reconnects.total` and `streaming.session_dedupe.success` boolean event.

sam: SDK changes: I'll add `X-Stream-Conn-Id: uuid4()` by default for all JS/Go/py streaming clients and expose a `resume` option that sends `X-Stream-Seq`. Will try to land before EOD.

anya: Good. Quick point: ensure quota-backend can accept an in-flight merge operation (i.e., move tokens from stale conn to new conn) — otherwise we'll still bill twice. Kevin, can you confirm?

kevin: Confirmed. I'll add a lightweight in-memory reconciliation in the quota aggregator for 30s windows; it's sticky per-customer and will emit an audit event we can surface in console logs.

maria: I'll wire the new metrics to the console and add a tooltip explaining heuristics. Also add a one-off CSV export to reconcile affected customers for billing ops.

anya: Who's owning the customer comms? We should proactively reach out to top 20 affected accounts and explain we're mitigating duplicates and will credit any overcharges.

sam: I can draft a short comms doc. cc @maria for which accounts to prioritize.

kevin: I'll open the PR for the heuristic + quota reconciliation and include unit tests and a feature flag `reconnect_dedupe_v1`. Deploy to canary first.

infra-bot: PR kevin/stream-reconnect-dedupe #421 merged into canary at 1856010200.

anya: Thanks. Let's also add a small log line when we apply the heuristic: `applied_reconnect_dedupe=true reason=short_window prior_conn_ts=...` so SRE can grep.

maria: Filed dashboard ticket: PLAT-764 "Reconnect penalty dashboard" and linked to PR #421.

kevin: ETA for prod enable behind flag: 24h after canary metrics look stable. I'll post a follow-up here.

anya: Nice work. Once flag flips, ops: run reconciliation script and generate credits for customers with clear duplicate events.

sam: Draft ready, will share in #customer-success when we have final list. :thumbsup:

kevin: FYI for follow-ups — need to decide default behavior for Private deployments (we should keep behavior same as hosted unless customer requests otherwise).

anya: Agreed. OK closing the loop, will monitor the `reconnect_penalty` metric.

maria: ping @kevin when you flip the flag so I can enable dashboard widgets.

kevin: Will do.
